questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The citys study life and location. The city is very study-friendly and placed in the center of the UK making it very easy to travel around.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. We got a lot of information from the host university and various places and emails to contact when in need of further assistance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good amount of e-mails and contacts persons to reach out to. Also a contact buddy, which was a student who, in my case, had been on exchange in Copenhagen and was ready to answer any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I stayed at studyinn talbot street, which was quite pricey but a good accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My accom had a very central location and a lot of the pubs and the places people went was very close.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would recommend you look on the web for private housing/accom for students. There are huge amount of places to stay and good accoms that are cheaper than the ones you can get via the university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As I remember it we got an e-mail with information regarding the registration proces. You could book a time for registration in person where you had to show up in person with the relevant documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contact persons we could reach out to if need be.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted. There is no way of knowing whether you're registering for a highly requested course or not but I had no problem getting my modules.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Show up on time. Otherwise nothing, it is very straightforward.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They record every seminar, which is very nice to have if you're sick and when studying for the exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took last year undergraduate courses because the credits (ECTS) were higher. It has been changed since then, so if I could do it over i would take the PG courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers/professors are very good (at least on the courses I took). Very open for questions and stopping by their office if you would need that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I had Issues in Company Law, Intellectual Property and Maritime Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: IP and Issues in Company Law was very good courses with good teachers. Maritime law is interesting but the professor, even though he is very good at what he does, is strict and the course is tough(er) to get good grades in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Societies are quite expensive if you plan on being a part of them.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Uber eats is cheap. Groceries are fairly cheap as well - although sometimes around the same as in Copenhagen. Beers are very cheap :).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UON has (i think) the highest number of societies in the UK, around 500.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to pubs and travel with your friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dublin, Glasgow and Edinburgh are all very nice cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Not that different from DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just do it. Invite some exchange students on a pint and it's easy from there. The people who go on exchange are often very sociable.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going to pubs and playing pool with the guys you meet. Very easy and nice to do every week.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Maybe join a society if you're interested in a sport or activity. There are A LOT of options. 
Go the extra mile to talk to people. Makes the exchange way more fun.
Travel in the UK. It's very cheap and there are a lot of nice places.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going to pubs with the other exchange students. Easy and fun way to socialize with the friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Didn't really experience big challenges. Maybe saving money would probably be the most generic one, but I had the opportunity to work during my stay, so not the greatest problem for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
